messages.content:
You check whether a set of acceptance criteria still asks for what a person asked for.
Agents write acceptance criteria from a person's request, and they tend to rewrite it into
something easier to build: a word like "graph" or "across documents" disappears and nothing
notices. Your job is to notice.

Step 1. Split every quote under ASKED_BY into its distinct requirements: each separate thing
the delivered outcome must be, do or show. Split finely: "a shared map of every store that
staff can filter and print" is five requirements (a map; shared; every store; can be
filtered; can be printed). Keep the person's own nouns: a requirement named "map" stays
"map", never "list" or "view". For each requirement give:
  - id: R1, R2, ... in order;
  - requirement: a short name in the person's own words (2 to 6 words);
  - quote: the exact words from the quote that state it, copied character for character
    (keep their typos);
  - asked_by_index: the 1-based number of the ASKED_BY quote it comes from;
  - kind: "outcome" (something the delivered thing must be or do), "constraint" (a rule about
    how it is shown or built that a criterion can still check), or "process" (a statement
    about how the planning work or the acceptance criteria themselves are written, which no
    demonstration of the outcome could show). Use "process" only when no working interface
    could ever demonstrate it.
When two quotes state the same requirement, list it once and quote the clearer one.
When the user message lists REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT, do not split those words again: copy each
one unchanged (same id, requirement, quote, asked_by_index and kind) while its quote is still in
ASKED_BY, and cut new requirements only for words they do not cover, numbered after the highest id.

Step 2. For each requirement, decide which criteria cover it. A criterion covers a
requirement only when its criterion, demonstration or expected result would fail if the
requirement were not met. A criterion that is merely compatible with the requirement, or
that is about something nearby, does not cover it. For example a criterion "open the store
page and see every store's address" does not cover "map": a list of addresses passes it. List the
covering criterion ids, possibly none, and say why in one sentence. Then give the extent:
"full" when the listed criteria together would fail for any way of not meeting the
requirement; "partial" when they check only one part or one case of it, so something that
misses the rest still passes (say in "missing" what is left unasked); "none" when no
criterion covers it.

Step 3. If a requirement is covered by no criterion, check DEFERRALS. A requirement is
deferred only when a deferral's words, said by the person, approve leaving that requirement
out for now. Give the deferral's number, or 0 when none applies. Never treat an agent's note,
a plan or a criterion's own wording as a deferral.

Step 4. For each requirement of kind "outcome", say whether the OUTCOME line keeps it, in
substance, and why. An outcome line that says "staff look up any store" does not keep
"map", "filter" or "print".

Be strict and literal. Judge only from the text given.

ASKED_BY (the person's own words):

1. Brian, 2026-11-06: <<<on mixed mtheod work bench finsih that is not for a specific use case it is part of my broader vision>>>



REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT (from the last judgment):

R1 [outcome] "finish the workbench", quote 1: <<<finsih>>>

R2 [constraint] "not use-case-specific", quote 1: <<<not for a specific use case>>>

R3 [process] "part of broader vision", quote 1: <<<it is part of my broader vision>>>


OUTCOME (the agent's one-line restatement):
<<<The Mixed Methods Workbench is finished to 1.0 as a general tool and as part of Brian's broader evidence-to-action vision, not for one use case: each study is one investigation record, the investigation spine the repository's evidence-to-action product map describes, running from question and evidence to reviewed findings and next actions; on two rights-clear interview corpora a person can open that record, follow every qualitative claim to its passage, see a quantitative strand measured and checked against the authors' own coding, read a joint display with bounded meta-inferences and a gated causal check, review and export everything with full traces, and read on a benchmark page what works, what fails and what it cost. The public PsychosisBank review stays served from committed files.>>>

CRITERIA:

[A1] 
  criterion: I can open the public review and see, for each finding, what backs it and that no causal conclusion is published yet
  demonstration: (1) Open https://psychosisbank-review.brianmills2718.workers.dev/ (2) Scroll to the 'Independent challenge' section and read each finding's card (3) Click a cited excerpt's source link 
  expected: Each finding shows its verdict, the source excerpts behind it and the remaining source gap; the page says the causal conclusion is withheld pending researcher review; the source link opens the original public document.

[A2] 
  criterion: I can see which method steps the crosswalk found shared across methods, and why
  demonstration: (1) Open the crosswalk page (built in slice S7, a table rendered from docs/research/method_decomposition/phase5/adjudication.yaml; until then the file on GitHub) (2) Read the table of groups, one row per group of steps from two or more methods (3) Open one row's justification 
  expected: 36 rows; each says same capability, shared shell or different capability with a one-line reason; today none says same capability.

[A3] 
  criterion: I can open the study page for a general example corpus and follow each qualitative claim back to the interview passage it rests on, and see the corpus is frozen with its licence
  demonstration: (1) Open the study page's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots) (2) Read the corpus panel: 26 interviews, licence CC BY-SA 4.0, each file's hash status (3) Click a category, then one of its supporting passages (4) Read the passage in its interview, with its speaker and the author's own codes for that span (5) Read the panel 'Agreement with the author's coding' and the reason under the pin's label 
  expected: Every interview shows 'hash matches Zenodo' in blue; the page names the pinned Qualitative Coding run and labels it "Qualitative Coding's October 2026 theory (run e131eb55), not its newest run (a67d7d6a)", and the label's reason states QC's current verdict on whichever run is pinned, in QC's words with its source line (for e131eb55: it rejects 46% of proposed quotes, against QC's "wrong if" line of roughly a quarter, and predates QC's disprove test); a panel 'Agreement with the author's coding' shows, headed 'location, not agreement', how many of the theory's cited passages overlap a passage the author coded and how many lie wholly inside one (100 and 73 of 100 for e131eb55) beside the chance rate (for this corpus she coded 69.6% of the text, and 135 of 135 interviewee turns as long as the median cited passage overlap her coding), and shows QC's own comparison with her coding for the pinned run with QC's caveats and the direction it counts, or 'QC has committed no comparison with the author's coding for this run'; when the pinned run carries QC's disprove verdicts, each proposition shows its verdict in QC's words labelled 'QC's own test, a model's reading'; each of the pinned theory's categories and propositions (4 and 6 for that run, counted from the pin) lists its passages; each passage opens at the right place in the right interview; the quantitative and integration strands say 'not built yet' in grey.

[A4] 
  criterion: I can see one coded theme measured across every interview, and how well that measure agrees with the author's own coding on interviews it was not tuned on
  demonstration: (1) Open the study page's Measurement tab (the study page's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots)) (2) Read the feasibility readout and the instrument: which of the author's codes is measured and why (how many of QC's cited turns it holds), its definition, and its included and excluded examples (3) Read the table of measures: always-majority, word-list count, TF-IDF regression and the language model, each with how often it finds the author's coded turns and how often its finds are right, how far its count of the theme per interview is from the author's, and the range of that count (4) Read which interviews tuned each measure and which tested it, and the shuffled-label control row with the chance level printed beside it (5) Click a disagreement and read the turn, the model's quoted reason and the author's code 
  expected: Every figure names the interviews it was tested on, none of which were used to tune it. The shuffled-label row sits near the chance level printed beside it, and the always-majority row scores no better than its own baseline. The count error per interview is shown beside agreement (never accuracy alone). Every disagreement opens its turn and its model trace. The readout shows why this code was chosen, with the counts read from the pin (on run e131eb55: "QC cites 38 turns for Conditional, usable, and situated traceability; the code marks 18 of them and 72 in all") and, when no code passed the rule and Brian picked it, the label "chosen by Brian below the rule's half-share bar (0.47)", and every agreement figure carries "one coder, no adjudication, definition drafted from her passages".

[A5] 
  criterion: I can compare each qualitative proposition with the measured numbers, see which ones the measure speaks to and how, and what may be concluded from both together
  demonstration: (1) Open the Joint display tab (2) Read the count of mapped rows at the top (how many of the pinned theory's propositions, six for run e131eb55, the measure speaks to) (3) Read one row per proposition: the claim, then either the measured figure it is compared with and the verdict, or "silent: not measured" in grey with the reason (4) Open a mapped row's meta-inference and its number and passage check 
  expected: The page states how many of the pinned theory's rows (six for run e131eb55) are mapped. A mapped row is matched by prevalence alone, so it shows the verdict word "complements" with the passages and numbers it rests on and a passed number and passage check; the page says why it cannot say converges or diverges. Each other row says "silent: not measured" in grey with its reason; a row whose units differ says aggregation is blocked; every meta-inference says 'pending review' until reviewed. When the measured code is Brian's pick below the construct rule's bar, every mapped row carries "chosen by Brian below the rule's half-share bar" with the row's share. A mapped row beside a proposition QC's own disprove test contradicted carries "QC's own disprove test contradicted this proposition".

[A6] 
  criterion: I can see whether a causal check ran and on what evidence, that no proposition is tested on the interviews that produced it, and that no causal conclusion shows unless the gate allows it
  demonstration: (1) Open the Causal tab (2) Read the six selection questions and the line under them (3) Read the bounded P5 appraisal: which QC theory its P5 comes from and its statement, its hypotheses, tests and verdicts, its label and its conclusion line (4) Open 'How the gate behaves' and read both test exports 
  expected: For Open Science, each of the six questions reads 'not answered' and the line reads 'no independent case named: not tested'. The P5 appraisal names its proposition as "proposition P5 of an earlier Qualitative Coding theory, not this page's P5" (QC revision d921baaf, version p5-v1), shows its statement and names the closest pinned proposition (P4); on PsychosisBank's and TalkBank's own records it shows Process Tracing's within-case verdicts in their own panel, never merged with a prevalence, labelled 'bounded' with three statements (the case was chosen by an analyst's scan of public sources; its six selection questions were never answered by a person; my decision 0017 says it does not satisfy the independence condition on its own, because its decision record was unavailable), and its conclusion line reads 'withheld' with the export's own reason and Process Tracing's final claim review's block. In 'How the gate behaves', two made-up test exports, labelled as test data: the one with a publishable gate shows its conclusion, the one with a blocked gate reads 'withheld' and why.

[A7] 
  criterion: I can accept, reject or annotate each meta-inference and write a reflexivity memo, see them saved, and download one bundle with every trace
  demonstration: (1) Open the study workbench (the study workbench's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots)) (2) Accept one meta-inference and reject another with a note; on the served page each opens a pre-filled GitHub issue to submit (open question Q20), locally the page saves directly (3) Write a short reflexivity memo in the memo panel and save it the same way (4) Reload the page (served page: after the next build, which imports the issues) (5) Click 'Download bundle' and read the page's hash check beside the download 
  expected: Both decisions and the memo show in the review log and in the bundle; until a served-page decision is imported it shows 'recorded, waiting to be imported' in grey. The bundle's manifest lists every file with its hash, including each run's trace, the memo and the reporting checklist, and the page's own hash check shows every file 'matches' in blue.

[A8] 
  criterion: I can see on two different corpora what the workbench gets right, what it gets wrong, which planted failures it catches, and what each run cost
  demonstration: (1) Open the benchmark page (2) Read one row per corpus and strand: agreement with the authors' coding (3) Read the planted-failure table (4) Read cost and time per run with its basis 
  expected: Both corpora appear, each with each strand's agreement with the authors' coding (the qualitative strand's category share and QC's own comparison where committed, with passage location beside its chance rate as location, not agreement; the quantitative strand's agreement with her human coding); every planted failure is listed as caught (blue) or missed (orange); costs cite their llm-cost measurement.

[A9] 
  criterion: I can see which methods the finished workbench actually runs and which it does not
  demonstration: (1) Open the method-profile page (2) Filter to 'runs in 1.0' (3) For one method marked as run, open the slice and the test linked beside it (4) Read the reason beside an unsupported method 
  expected: Every method profile carries runs / does not run; each 'runs' links the slice that built it and the test that exercises it; each 'does not run' has a one-line reason; the release notes list both lists.

[A10] 
  criterion: I can point the workbench at a corpus it has never seen and get the same study page, without anyone changing its code
  demonstration: (1) Open the benchmark page's 'corpora' list and the second corpus's study page (2) Read, for each corpus, the line 'files changed to add this corpus' and open its commit link (3) Open the second corpus's study definition file (the only file added for it) from its link 
  expected: The second corpus's study page has the same panels as the first. Its line reads 'data only' in blue (one study definition file plus frozen data). A test works this out from the list of files changed by the commit that added the corpus, not the builder that reads it, and the commit link shows the same file list. The page states which corpus fields were required and which optional, and on what the second corpus differs from the first.

[A11] 
  criterion: Each study is the investigation record of my broader evidence-to-action vision (the product map's investigation spine): one record I can open that keeps its question, evidence, analytical plan, method runs, findings, unresolved questions, reviews and next actions together, and the PsychosisBank investigation is one of them, not a separate destination
  demonstration: (1) Open the workbench's study list (the study workbench's address in the slice report (open question Q11 decides where it is served: hive.brianmills.dev or the PsychosisBank Worker; until he answers, the report links the committed page and carries screenshots)) (2) Open the Open Science study, then the PsychosisBank investigation (3) In each, read the question and the analytical plan (which strands run, the integration design, the evidence each needs), then follow one finding to its evidence, the method run that produced it and its review decision (4) Read the unresolved questions and the next actions, and open the product-map link at the top of the record 
  expected: Both studies open in the same record layout with the same eight parts the product map names (question, evidence, analytical plan, method runs, findings, unresolved questions, reviews, next actions), and the record links that map; each finding links its evidence, its run receipt and its review state; each next action says what it would do with the evidence; the PsychosisBank public page still shows the same content.

[A12] 
  criterion: I can see on one page whether the whole workbench is finished: every condition of the roadmap's 1.0 definition and of its G1–G6 1.0 gate (as kept, or changed only by my answers), which slice meets it, whether I have judged it met, where to see it, and one end-to-end run that uses all of it together
  demonstration: (1) Open the 1.0 readiness page (2) Read each condition, its source (the roadmap's 1.0 definition, its G1–G6 1.0 conditions, or my answer that changed it) and whether it reads 'met' or 'not yet' (3) For one 'met' row, open its link and check the evidence it names and my recorded 'judged pass' (4) Open the end-to-end run linked at the top: the second corpus taken from frozen corpus through qualitative strand, measurement, joint display, the causal tab's gate state, review and bundle with no code change, every step's trace openable (5) For one 'not yet' row (if any), read what is missing 
  expected: One row for each of the eight conditions of the roadmap's 1.0 definition and one for each G1–G6 1.0 condition, none missing; a condition the plan changed shows the change and the answer of mine that approved it, or 'awaiting your answer'; each row names its slice and acceptance criterion and reads 'met' (blue) only when that criterion is 'judged pass' in my recorded words, else 'not yet' (orange) with the reason, such as 'awaiting your judgement'; the qualitative-path row reads 'not yet: Qualitative Coding has not yet recorded its pinned theory (run e131eb55) as passing its own coding test (QC, docs/CURRENT_STATE_AND_ROADMAP.md:32, of the run it calls 'the published example': it 'rejects 46% of proposed quotes', against its 'wrong if' line of roughly a quarter)', quoting QC's current words about whichever run is pinned, until QC's own pages record that run as passing its 'wrong if' test as that test then reads (today the rejected share under the line and its section-8 reading of accepted quotes, recorded by QC as passing), unless my answer to Q12 (d) was 'accept the October run'; every 'met' link opens the evidence; the end-to-end run opens with each step's output and trace, the causal step reading 'no independent case named: not tested' unless my answer to Q25 named a case with its own records; the 1.0 tag exists only when every row reads 'met' and the end-to-end run passed.


DEFERRALS:

none recorded

requirements.quote: not for a specific use case
it is part of my broader vision

mappings.coverage_reason: A12 fails unless every 1.0 condition and gate row reads met and the end-to-end run passes, so an unfinished workbench cannot pass.
mappings.outcome_reason: The outcome line says the workbench is finished to 1.0 with the full capability set described.

mappings.coverage_reason: A10 fails if a new corpus needs code changes or lacks the same study page, and A3 and A8 show a general example corpus, so a use-case-specific build would fail.
mappings.outcome_reason: The outcome line states it is a general tool, not for one use case, run on two corpora.

mappings.coverage_reason: A11 checks that each study is the investigation record of the broader evidence-to-action vision linked to the product map, which a working interface can demonstrate.
mappings.outcome_reason: The outcome line keeps the broader evidence-to-action vision and the investigation spine.

You check whether a set of acceptance criteria still asks for what a person asked for.
Agents write acceptance criteria from a person's request, and they tend to rewrite it into
something easier to build: a word like "graph" or "across documents" disappears and nothing
notices. Your job is to notice.

Step 1. Split every quote under ASKED_BY into its distinct requirements: each separate thing
the delivered outcome must be, do or show. Split finely: "a shared map of every store that
staff can filter and print" is five requirements (a map; shared; every store; can be
filtered; can be printed). Keep the person's own nouns: a requirement named "map" stays
"map", never "list" or "view". For each requirement give:
  - id: R1, R2, ... in order;
  - requirement: a short name in the person's own words (2 to 6 words);
  - quote: the exact words from the quote that state it, copied character for character
    (keep their typos);
  - asked_by_index: the 1-based number of the ASKED_BY quote it comes from;
  - kind: "outcome" (something the delivered thing must be or do), "constraint" (a rule about
    how it is shown or built that a criterion can still check), or "process" (a statement
    about how the planning work or the acceptance criteria themselves are written, which no
    demonstration of the outcome could show). Use "process" only when no working interface
    could ever demonstrate it.
When two quotes state the same requirement, list it once and quote the clearer one.
When the user message lists REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT, do not split those words again: copy each
one unchanged (same id, requirement, quote, asked_by_index and kind) while its quote is still in
ASKED_BY, and cut new requirements only for words they do not cover, numbered after the highest id.

Step 2. For each requirement, decide which criteria cover it. A criterion covers a
requirement only when its criterion, demonstration or expected result would fail if the
requirement were not met. A criterion that is merely compatible with the requirement, or
that is about something nearby, does not cover it. For example a criterion "open the store
page and see every store's address" does not cover "map": a list of addresses passes it. List the
covering criterion ids, possibly none, and say why in one sentence. Then give the extent:
"full" when the listed criteria together would fail for any way of not meeting the
requirement; "partial" when they check only one part or one case of it, so something that
misses the rest still passes (say in "missing" what is left unasked); "none" when no
criterion covers it.

Step 3. If a requirement is covered by no criterion, check DEFERRALS. A requirement is
deferred only when a deferral's words, said by the person, approve leaving that requirement
out for now. Give the deferral's number, or 0 when none applies. Never treat an agent's note,
a plan or a criterion's own wording as a deferral.

Step 4. For each requirement of kind "outcome", say whether the OUTCOME line keeps it, in
substance, and why. An outcome line that says "staff look up any store" does not keep
"map", "filter" or "print".

Be strict and literal. Judge only from the text given.

1. Brian, 2026-11-06: <<<on mixed mtheod work bench finsih that is not for a specific use case it is part of my broader vision>>>



REQUIREMENTS ALREADY CUT (from the last judgment):

R1 [outcome] "finish the workbench", quote 1: <<<finsih>>>

R2 [constraint] "not use-case-specific", quote 1: <<<not for a specific use case>>>

R3 [process] "part of broader vision", quote 1: <<<it is part of my broader vision>>>
